title: Returned Payments and Income Records Requests on Long-Term Hardship Holds
content:
**Payments desk Q&A — Hardship and Protective Holds.** When updated household income records are asked for before a status review of a running Long-Term Hardship Hold, the income returned-payment allowance depends on the payments returned on the held account dated less than six whole months before today, as booked in the account's money history under Placed Consumer Accounts. Whole months are the difference in calendar months between the date and today, less one when today's day of the month is smaller than the date's day of the month. The allowance is added once to the days allowed for the income records:

| Returned payments in the period | Income returned-payment allowance |
|---|---|
| At least the repeat-return count of 2 | 4 calendar days (income repeat-return days) |
| Exactly 1 | 2 calendar days (income single-return days) |
| None | Nothing |

**How many returns trigger the larger figure?** Two or more: 4 days. One return gives 2 days.

**Is a return from seven months ago counted?** No; it is not dated less than six whole months before today.

**Example (hypothetical).** Today is 10 October; one payment on the held account was returned on 11 April. The calendar months are 6, and today's day (10) is smaller than 11, so the whole months are 5: the return counts. One return: 2 calendar days are added.
